current_findings.finding: Full heuristic-only warmup with block reward 0.15 produced the strongest robust model in that batch; lower/higher nearby coefficients and mixture schedules did not surpass it.

Widening the post-flatten projection 512→1024 is a breakthrough for late warmup trajectories at seed 42: it beat the prior baseline 5/5 on Combined-X, Combined-O, and aggregate, with means 0.504/0.232/0.524 versus 0.358/0.150/0.437. True LR decay and batch256 were dead ends for the ticket because their aggregate means regressed; no candidate reached sustained 0.60 on both Combined sides.

Across both final-attempt matched seeds, reallocating conserved expected opening exposure from (.30 X,.30 O) to (.00 X,.60 O) was a replicated dead end: Combined-O fell by .082 and .086, aggregate fell by .024 and .085, and Offensive-X fell by .116 and .274 versus same-seed controls. Neither treatment had any final-five Combined checkpoint at or above .60, so the immutable seed-42 champion remained not opponent-pool ready.

Persistent entropy 0.010 remains a single-seed breakthrough and diagnostic champion (Combined-X/O/aggregate 0.604/0.558/0.650667), but it is not opponent-pool ready and loses Offensive-X. Fixed entropy 0.0075, a 0.010-through-75%-then-0.005 schedule, and the final 0.010-through-90%-then-0.0075 schedule were mature dead ends; the final schedule scored 0.042/0.046/0.287 and trailed both baseline and entropy010 0/5 at every aligned primary trajectory. Both scheduled runs lacked parent-like Combined capability before annealing began, reinforcing sharply nonlinear/GPU-sensitive optimization paths rather than smooth entropy interpolation. Max_iterations=3 is exhausted without a ready model.

historical_summaries: extended-heuristic-training, 2 runs, Jul 18–19 2026 — dead end: Early heuristic-heavy training was highly asymmetric and extension did not repair the weak side.
all-heuristic-curriculum, 2 runs, Jul 20 2026 — dead end: Substantially greater/all-heuristic exposure was a dead end in both variants.

reproduction-and-forgetting, 3 runs, Jul 20–21 2026 — finding: The original short regimen reproduced strong mean performance, while snapshot continuation sharply forgot offensive-first play; a fresh longer schedule largely recovered the mean but retained a zero worst side.

potential-reward-shaping, 6 runs, Jul 21–24 2026 — finding: Unshaped training produced the best controlled terminal mean; shaping strength and defensive weighting failed to improve the weakest matchup.
warmup-duration-control, 2 runs, Jul 24 2026 — finding: The nominal longer reproduction strongly beat the shortened warmup, rejecting the idea that shortening warmup was harmless.
combined-heuristic-shaping, 3 runs, Jul 26–27 2026 — dead end: Combined-only heuristic training remained brittle; removing shaping modestly improved mean, while defense-biased shaping did not.
full-combined-defense-weight, 4 runs, Jul 28–31 2026 — finding: At full duration, defense weight 1.5 was the useful shaping setting; weight 2 raised mean slightly but reduced worst-side robustness.

defensive-opening-curriculum, 4 runs, Aug 1–3 2026 — dead end: The initial opening-curriculum variants did not consistently improve robustness; the no-opening annealed/shaped variant had the best mean in this group.
fixed-defensive-curriculum-shaping, 2 runs, Aug 3 2026 — finding: After the curriculum fix, slight shaping improved the pair but absolute robustness remained low.
center-mask-shaping-and-lr, 3 runs, Aug 4 2026 — finding: Annealed learning rate plus slight shaping was a meaningful recovery over both center-masked controls.

mistake-rate-block-reward-interaction, 6 runs, Aug 4–6 2026 — finding: Without block reward, starting mistake rate 0.7/0.5 beat 0.3; adding block reward 0.5 collapsed performance despite high collected block reward.
block-reward-coefficient-sweep, 3 runs, Aug 7 2026 — finding: The controlled sweep located a moderate optimum at 0.25; 0.4 collapsed and 0.1 was intermediate.
long-block25-refinements, 3 runs, Aug 8 2026 — finding: At 0.25 and 15.36M steps, slight shaping hurt while opening probability 0.4 modestly improved the mean.

block20-opening-retries, 4 runs, Aug 16–17 2026 — finding: Reducing block reward to 0.20 improved long-run robustness, and opening probability 0.4 slightly raised mean but slightly lowered worst side in completed retries.

scope.chronology_basis: MLflow meta.yaml start_time; run-name dates are not assumed reliable

global_caveats: All terminal evaluations use finite games per side and most variants have one seed, so close differences can be sampling noise.

Six status-1 runs—df624486aa56409d8f50269333723a28, f9c8f998888648a0ba59c78757125476, 0c572fdacc98462798966e1aad118c63, a6eb2d709e8e4adfba0ee5f4deb9be06, 1f9a5292b74e47ada012c9ba6a8e7246, and 099be2bb21fb48bc83980bc2ef6cb38a—are incomplete and are never treated as terminal rankings.
Metric schemas evolved: early runs omit episode lengths and some aggregates, so absence is not interpreted as zero.
Cross-group chronology often changes multiple parameters, curriculum implementations, or loaded snapshots; causal claims are restricted to close within-group controls.

patterns.interpretation: The highest historical mean run was side-specialized, and the open0.375 run improved Offensive-O while collapsing Combined and Offensive-X; balanced comparisons must inspect every policy/side cell and the weakest Combined side.
patterns.name: Mean performance is a poor proxy for robustness

patterns.interpretation: Collecting more shaped block reward is negatively associated with game strength at high coefficients; even with coefficient fixed at 0.15, the highest late block-reward mean in the opening sweep belonged to open0.375, whose Combined and aggregate performance was worst. Proxy reward must remain subordinate to external wins.
patterns.name: Block reward has a non-monotonic optimum and proxy-reward risk

patterns.interpretation: Shaping hurt in clean/near-clean comparisons more often than it helped; the corrected-curriculum improvement coincided with a learning-rate change.
patterns.name: Potential shaping is context-sensitive and usually negative

patterns.interpretation: Weight 1.5 gives the best robustness of this controlled sequence; weight 2 chases mean at the expense of the weakest cell.
patterns.name: Defense weight 1.5 is better than slight unbiased shaping, but does not solve side brittleness

patterns.interpretation: Older probability-0.4 regimens showed small mean gains, but the controlled wideproj 0.325–0.375 sweep did not beat the open0.30 champion. Open0.35 was closest at seed 42 yet matched seed 43 reduced Combined-O and Offensive-O. Defensive-opening dose is a seed-sensitive mean/side tradeoff, not a reliable weak-side solution.
patterns.name: Defensive openings help modestly only after the core regimen is sound

patterns.interpretation: Annealed LR rescued shaped center-mask training historically, but on the block-0.15 warmup regimen true 3e-4→1e-4 decay raised Combined-X/O while lowering aggregate from 0.437 to 0.427 and Offensive-X from 0.726 to 0.520; schedule transfer cannot be assumed.
patterns.name: Learning-rate schedule effects are regimen-dependent

patterns.interpretation: Snapshot-pool continuation requires checkpoint selection and anti-forgetting evaluation rather than assuming terminal improvement.
patterns.name: Longer or continued training can forget rather than monotonically improve

patterns.interpretation: At seed 42, widening only the post-flatten hidden projection 512→1024 raised final-five Combined-X/O/aggregate by +0.146/+0.082/+0.087 and beat baseline 5/5. The exact seed-43 control then scored 0.410/0.182/0.462 versus the champion's 0.504/0.232/0.524, so the gain is promising but seed-sensitive and not a replicated universal architecture effect.
patterns.name: Projection capacity improved one seed but requires multi-seed confirmation

patterns.interpretation: Corrected decay and batch256 improved selected O-side signals while regressing aggregate/offense; open0.375 improved Offensive-O but collapsed Combined-X/O, and seed43 open0.35 improved aggregate/X cells while reducing both target O cells. Weak-side progress must be gated jointly with Combined-X/O, aggregate, and all six cells.
patterns.name: Weak-side defensive gains can trade against broad offense

patterns.interpretation: The same architecture/regimen varies by roughly 0.05–0.09 in key final-five means across seeds, while an opening-dose effect can change sign. Promotion decisions require matched seeds and should not treat small single-seed deltas as causal.
patterns.name: Training-seed variance is decision-scale in late warmup

patterns.interpretation: At fixed expected overall opening exposure, moving all designed-opening attempts to O reduced Combined-O at both seeds (-.082/-.086), shortened Combined-O games (-1.140/-.296), damaged Offensive-X (-.116/-.274), and reduced aggregate (-.024/-.085). Side targeting alone does not make the existing generic threat generator an effective weak-side curriculum.
patterns.name: O-only generic opening exposure amplified side brittleness across matched seeds

prior_champion.reason: Entropy010 beat the immutable champion at all five aligned late checkpoints on Combined-X, Combined-O, and aggregate, raising means from 0.504/0.232/0.524 to 0.604/0.558/0.650667; five of six cell means improved.

champion.readiness_caveat: Champion status is not opponent-pool readiness. Combined-X sustained >=0.60 (mean 0.604; 4/5 checkpoints), but Combined-O did not (mean 0.558; 1/5). Aggregate mean 0.650667 had only 1/5 checkpoints >=0.6833; Offensive-X 0.664 and Offensive-O 0.564 also missed their 0.90/0.60 gates. Attempt-2 entropy refinements and the final 90%-hold/0.0075 schedule were mature regressions, so max_iterations=3 is exhausted with no model authorized for opponent-pool training.

rejected_challengers.reason: Attempt-1 sideaware-xmist20, dilated-rf13, block125, and gae098 failed baseline movement. Attempt-2 entropy0075 and entlate010to005 were below both immutable baseline and entropy010 at all five aligned late checkpoints for Combined-X, Combined-O, and aggregate. The final 90%-hold/0.0075 schedule also trailed both references 0/5 on all three primaries, with means 0.042/0.046/0.287 and Offensive-X 0.678 below the >=0.742 refinement guard.

champion.selection_criterion: Best completed warmup under aligned balanced evidence: persistent Combined-X/O and aggregate movement first, then all six paired rate/length cells. Entropy010 remains the diagnostic champion after three failed entropy refinements because its primary gains are large and 5/5 aligned, although it remains a one-seed result, failed readiness, and is not authorized for opponent-pool training.

evaluation_requirements: Primary warmup-readiness metrics remain aligned final-window Combined-X and Combined-O win rates paired with avg_episode_length; opponent-pool transition requires final-five mean >=0.60 and at least three checkpoints >=0.60 on both sides.
Secondary aggregate floor remains eval/average_win_rate >=0.6833 as both final-five mean and at least three checkpoints; report all six component cells rather than aggregate alone.
Preserve Offensive-X >=0.90 for full proficiency and require >=0.742 for any entropy refinement's mechanism guard; longer games count only when win rate improves.
A candidate's Combined-X, Combined-O, and aggregate means must exceed immutable baseline 0.504/0.232/0.524 and beat it at least 3/5 aligned late checkpoints.
Use matched replicated seeds only after a candidate passes the predeclared promising gate; observed training-seed and optimization-path variance is decision-scale.
Never rank partial runs against completed terminal results, and treat the shared 59-point mistake-rate history as a documented equality-boundary logger omission rather than a 15.36M value.

prioritized.caveat: Entropy010 is still the strongest observed diagnostic run but failed Combined-O, Offensive-X/O, and aggregate proficiency and was not replication-eligible.
prioritized.design: Any continuation requires a new ticket with a new hypothesis and unchanged readiness gates, not a fourth retry or weakened threshold.
prioritized.direction: Close raise_warmup_performance_4 without another automated retry and do not begin opponent-pool training; max_iterations=3 is exhausted and entropy010 remains diagnostic-only.
prioritized.hypothesis: None of the three iterations produced sustained >=0.60 Combined proficiency on both sides. The final candidate's 0.042/0.046/0.287 primary means and 0/5 relative checkpoint wins provide mature negative evidence, not an immature run that warrants HOLD.

prioritized.caveat: These are single realized GPU trajectories, so they decisively reject promotion but do not identify a universal entropy law.
prioritized.design: Predeclare multiple matched seeds or deterministic settings, compare capability at schedule-change boundaries, log all entropy values, and avoid claiming a terminal anneal caused an earlier divergence.
prioritized.direction: If future entropy research is opened under a new ticket, first design matched replications or deterministic diagnostics that can separate schedule effects from optimization-path variance.
prioritized.hypothesis: The successful persistent-0.010 run and two schedule runs shared nominal 0.010 entropy before their anneal boundaries, yet both schedule runs lacked Combined competence before annealing began; nonlinear/GPU-sensitive trajectory divergence dominates simple dose interpolation.

prioritized.caveat: The results reject these realized configurations for promotion but not every possible entropy schedule.
prioritized.design: Do not perform another nearby fixed-dose or schedule sweep without a qualitatively new variance-control or mechanism-identification design.
prioritized.direction: Keep fixed entropy 0.0075, 0.010-through-75%-then-0.005, and 0.010-through-90%-then-0.0075 as negative controls rather than nearby sweep candidates.
prioritized.hypothesis: All three mature refinements failed relative and absolute Combined gates; the two scheduled candidates had no parent-like broad capability at their anneal boundaries, and the fixed midpoint almost eliminated Combined wins.

prioritized.caveat: Qualitatively redesigned curricula or architectures are not ruled out, but must be isolated and cannot exceed the successful architecture ceiling.
prioritized.design: Restore role-neutral 0.7→0.1 mistakes, undilated convolutions, block 0.15, and GAE 0.95 in any future isolated mechanism test.
prioritized.direction: Keep role-aware easier-opponent mistakes, RF13 dilation, block reward 0.125, GAE 0.98, and O-only generic defensive openings as negative controls rather than retry candidates.
prioritized.hypothesis: Their mature primary regressions indicate weakened realistic pressure/local tactical features/defensive credit, increased estimator noise, or ineffective side targeting.

prioritized.caveat: The omission does not make otherwise complete FINISHED runs immature.
prioritized.design: If production changes are later in scope, log the terminal scheduled rate before boundary return; meanwhile never reinterpret 0.11 as a 15.36M sample.
prioritized.direction: Fix or explicitly account for equality-boundary mistake-rate logging in future evidence contracts.
prioritized.hypothesis: Baseline, entropy010, both attempt-2 runs, and the attempt-3 candidate have 59 train/mistake_rate points ending at 15.104M while target evaluation and block reward have 60 through 15.36M, establishing callback ordering rather than missing training.

prioritized.caveat: Checkpoint selection is not permission to begin self-play and can overfit the same 100-game evaluations.
prioritized.design: Evaluate every snapshot on all policy/side cells, retain Pareto-optimal checkpoints, and compare continuation with versus without fixed heuristic rehearsal.
prioritized.direction: Only after both Combined sides meet readiness, add anti-forgetting checkpoint selection before self-play continuation.
prioritized.hypothesis: Minimum-cell checkpoint selection plus heuristic rehearsal may prevent the offensive forgetting seen in prior snapshot continuation.
